outcomes: Upon successful completion of the program, students will be able to demonstrate developmentally appropriate curriculum and explain principles and practices pertaining to child development.
Upon successful completion of the program, students will be able to compile topics concerning the child, family, and community, and will be able to demonstrate pediatric CPR and first aid.
Upon successful completion of the program, students will be able to compose observations and assessments, of children from infancy to adolescents considering culture and typical and atypical needs.

Upon successful completion of the program, the master teacher will be able to design a care plan for the needs of infant and toddlers or special education children commensurate to their specialization.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to differentiate the historical perspectives, theories, and methods used within the human services discipline.
Explain the major problems and issues in the disciplines in their contemporary, historical and geographical contexts.

Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to analyze social problems and policies, and identify and evaluate services that meet the needs of disadvantaged populations. They will also be able to examine and argue the societal factors that contribute to social service needs.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will implement cultural competence and interpersonal and social skills when interacting with diverse populations.

Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to interpret the legal and professional responsibilities associated with a career in human services. They will also be able to demonstrate ethical decision-making steps within the human services system and specifically when dealing with case management.
